title: Otis and Orla's Charm Chase
markdown:
The sun, like a sleepy marmot, was just peeking over the craggy peaks of Hazelhowe. Down in the echoing ravines, young Otis the wizard hummed a wobbly tune. His fingers polished the Hazelhowe Charm: a small pearly stone glowing with captured moonlight, smooth and cool as a pebble from a secret stream.

“Almost there, you shimmery thing.” Burnt-toast hair flopped into his eyes. Today was the Charm-Polishing Contest. He wanted the absolute best polish. Not win-win. The best gleam. A dewdrop on a spiderweb, reflecting all the colours of the morning sky.

A giggle like tiny wind chimes. Ears twitching. Orla, the young witch from the other side of the ravine, moonlight braids dancing like silver ribbons, boots soft on moss.

“Ready, Otis?” Bright as a robin’s song. She held up her own charm, dazzling inner light, a captured rainbow swirled inside.

“As I’ll ever be.” He puffed out his chest. Dust from his waistcoat. “Mine will gleam like a dewdrop on a spiderweb.”

“Mine will shine like a star in a puddle.” A friendly challenge in curious eyes. Good rivals. Always pushing each other.

They stood side by side. Charms gleamed under the soft morning sun. Air thrummed with quiet magic. Then a blur of emerald green and high-pitched giggles. A tiny winged creature, no bigger than Otis’s thumb, wings like spun dandelion fluff, snatched the Hazelhowe Charm from its velvet stand.

“Hey.” Otis jumped back.

“My charm.” Orla’s smile vanished like mist.

The Whisperwind Sprite giggled like tiny bells shaken hard and fluttered away, a streak of green into the shadowed mouths of the ravines.

Otis’s knees felt wobbly, jelly in the sun. A familiar knot: things going wrong, leaving him small.

“That’s it.” Orla’s chin high, determination like a sturdy oak. “We have to get it back. The Elder Willow judges are waiting. Contest by sundown. They won’t wait forever.” Shadows already stretching.

They set off. Otis trailed a bit, eyes in leafy shadows. A patch of moss that seemed to sigh contentedly. A large grumpy badger in a waistcoat of green moss sat in their path, whiskers twitching like tiny antennae.

“Halt,” grumbled Grizzle, voice like pebbles downhill. “No one passes without a proper greeting and perhaps a song. Or a juicy worm.”

Orla stepped forward, graceful. “Good day, Grizzle. We’re looking for a stolen charm. Very important.” Sweet as honey.

Grizzle scowled. “Important things are often misplaced. Especially by forgetful sprites. Always after something shiny.” A disgruntled sniff.

Otis, usually shy, remembered his manners. Shaky but clear. “It’s very kind of you to guard this path. The air smells of damp earth and sweet clover. Like after a gentle rain. And your moss waistcoat is a wonderful shade of green.” His trick: noticing the small pleasant things.

Grizzle blinked. Stopped grumbling. No one usually noticed his path. Or his waistcoat. “Well. The sprite went that way.” He nudged toward a narrow tunnel almost hidden by vines. “Be warned. The Moon-Moths there play tricks with light. A flighty bunch.”

The tunnel grew cooler, faint mushrooms. Tiny lights dancing: Moon-Moths, wings dusted with moon-sparkle, giggling in soft whispers, weaving patterns that led everywhere and nowhere. A kaleidoscope.

This way. No, this way. Otis felt the old fear of not knowing which path. The tunnel seemed to stretch forever.

Orla stopped. “Look.” The moths had stopped dancing. They were forming a shape: a rough map of the ravine. A small blinking X in the centre.

“That’s where the sprite must have taken it.” Curiosity sparked. Fear fading.

The map showed two paths. One easier, winding toward sun-drenched berries. The other dark and overgrown. The easy path tempted Otis. Quicker. Less scary. Grab those berries, have his own charm, no one would know he had not won properly.

Orla saw the overgrown path more clearly. “The sprite wouldn’t go for easy. It likes hidden places. But that path looks rough and thorny.” A small selfish thought: perhaps just take the berries.

Otis saw her hesitation. He remembered Grizzle’s warning. How much Orla wanted to win. A new strength. “No. We came this far. Together. We need to follow the sprite.” He pointed to the dark path. “We’ll go that way.”

Surprised, then a warm smile. “You’re right, Otis. Together.”

Shadowy tangle of gnarled roots. Wind like secrets. Scritch-scratch of unseen creatures. Drip of water. A small clearing in eerie greenish light. In the centre, the mischievous sprite juggling the Hazelhowe Charm, spinning, flashing like a tiny star. It giggled when it saw them, tossed the charm higher, winked.

Otis reached into his pouch. A small smooth grey pebble, ordinary as a river stone. Hand steady. “Look, little sprite. A stone for your collection. So smooth it feels like river water flowing over your fingers.”

The sprite paused, eyed the pebble, then the flashing charm. Tiny head tilted.

Orla took out a tiny sparkling sugar crystal, glittering like a miniature diamond. “And this is for trading. It tastes like sunshine and sweet dreams.”

Eyes widened. Shiny, tasty things. A squeal of delight. The charm dropped with a soft plink onto the moss. The sprite darted for the sugar crystal. Otis scooped up the charm.

The forest seemed to sigh. Damp earth and sweet clover.

They raced back, hearts like woodpeckers. Sun dipping, orange and purple. They burst into the clearing where the Elder Willow stood, ancient branches drooping, leaves whispering.

“We have it.” Otis held up the gleaming charm.

“We found it.” Orla’s moonlight braids bounced.

The Elder Willow’s leaves rustled like quiet applause. The judges—a wise old owl with amber eyes, a dignified stag—nodded. Since neither had polished perfectly alone, they were both awarded first place. They shared a long silken banner of shimmering blue. Their charms glowed side by side. Otis no longer felt that wobbly fear. He felt a steady quiet confidence, and Orla’s elbow bumping his, as if to say the polish could wait.
characters: Otis (young wizard who notices small pleasant things), Orla (a witch with moonlight braids)
author: StoryGen Community
